title: Final authority remains outside SWARM
context: Multi-agent/model workers can disagree, hallucinate, collude or fail.
options: SWARM produces candidates/evidence; JUDGE/LAW control release
decision: SWARM is not final truth authority; JUDGE/LAW/release policy govern authoritative output.
why: prevents majority popularity from becoming truth
consequences: release can freeze despite confident agents
rollback: requires explicit governance/spec change; not implementation-only decision

title: UI is presentation, not authority
context: Human-facing UX needs simplification, modes, animation and role-specific visibility.
options: UI state can optimistically define success
UI reflects backend truth; backend enforces authority
decision: UI may present/request but cannot define truth, lower verification, mask FREEZE or substitute authorization.

title: One authoritative output or freeze
context: Internal reasoning may retain multiple candidate paths.
options: show all candidates as equal answers
collapse to one governed result or freeze/silence
decision: Only one legal authoritative final output may release; unresolved conflict remains internal or blocks release.
consequences: some tasks end in FREEZE/no final answer
supersedes: earlier presentation concepts that could imply multiple finals

title: Conflict memory branches instead of destructive overwrite
context: New learning can contradict verified memory or prior law.
options: preserve branches/provenance and resolve through proof/simulation
decision: Conflict is preserved as explicit branches until governed resolution.
why: prevents poisoned update deleting valid history

title: Lo2 learning cannot silently self-modify authoritative kernels
context: Lo2 is designed to synthesize and evolve intelligence from verified history.
options: versioned candidate evolution with governed promotion/rollback
decision: Lo2 may propose/evolve/package intelligence, but authoritative promotion is versioned, verified and governed.
supersedes: earlier silent Lo2 kernel update vision

title: Current DOC-C build scope is not the entire NEXY vision
context: Source contains current build plus future Sovereign/Game/NCF/Robotics systems.
options: treat every source object as current required build
preserve future objects but gate promotion into DOC-C
decision: Future architecture remains queryable/source-valid but is not current DOC-C obligation unless explicitly promoted.
consequences: implementation may exist out of current scope without becoming required
absence of future feature is not current FAIL

title: Evidence is exact-revision and environment bound
context: Tests/evidence from previous commits can become stale after code/schema changes.
options: bind each proof to exact commit/environment/claim
decision: Evidence only proves the exact revision/environment/claim it records.
consequences: new HEAD may require rerunning gates
historical evidence remains useful but not current PASS
rollback: would weaken DOC-E evidence discipline and is not allowed by current governance

title: Failure is first-class state, not hidden fallback
context: Dependencies, proofs and state transitions can fail or remain uncertain.
options: surface explicit error/FREEZE/DEGRADED/STOP according to law
decision: Blocking failure remains visible and affects authoritative state; fallback must be explicit and governed.
consequences: availability may reduce under integrity failure

title: REQUIRES is a DAG; governance edges are separate
context: Architecture relationships include requires, governs, observes, secures, recovers and calls.
options: separate semantic relation types and keep REQUIRES acyclic
decision: REQUIRES represents build/task prerequisites and must remain acyclic; control/governance relations use other edge types.

title: Implementation presence is evidence class E0 only
context: Large repositories make it easy to confuse code existence with completed behavior.
decision: Implementation Map proves navigation/presence only. Verdict remains NOT_EVALUATED until requirement/test/evidence analysis.
